name: incident-response
description: Alert-triggered incident lifecycle template: triage -> debounce (confirm-live is a bare wait_s:120 timer — no live check, it exists only to ride out alert flapping) -> correlate with a 3-way verdict -> complementary gate pair (false-alarm arm tunes the alert rule; incident arm mitigates) -> machine-validated recovery probe -> resiliency retro -> merge-gated converge -> evidence-gated close. run_context seeds (ALL required): 'alert' = the trigger text as reported (alert name, hosts, time); 'sweep_cmd' = your alerting adapter command. ADAPTER CONTRACT for sweep_cmd: a command that lists currently-firing alerts, honoring '--match <regex>' (match on labels/summary; when --match is OMITTED the match regex is read from the scratch file 'incident.match' under the scratch root — never 'all') and '--expect fire|clear' where exit 0 = condition holds, exit 1 = it does not, exit 2 = probe broken. Example: 'python3 my_sweep.py'. Tracking is a scratch 'ticket.md' stand-in - swap in your tracker CLI (gh issue, jira, bd) in the goals. The scratch root /tmp/incident-response-example is shared handoff state: run ONE incident at a time, or per-run-isolate the paths (and the recovery-probe argv) for production. The recovery gate releases only on TWO CONSECUTIVE adapter-exit-0 polls to ride out flapping: a re-fire (exit 1) zeroes the counter, and a broken probe (adapter exit 2, or a missing verify_cmd.txt) zeroes it STICKY and writes prev_poll_broken + probe_broken + loud stderr plus a bounded incident-diagnostic.json record in the run dir (incident_id = run id, event/marker = probe_broken, probe_exit = 2; the same JSON also appears in the native parked stdout_tail) WITHOUT counting — so the clear that immediately follows a broken poll can NEVER release the gate and probe_broken stays written until a genuine two-clear release deletes it; a broken probe is never reportable as incident-clear. Flag readings, one each: clear_ticks = banked CONSECUTIVE adapter-exit-0 polls (any non-zero poll writes 0); prev_poll_broken = the immediately-preceding poll was broken, deleted by the next healthy poll, and a healthy poll that finds it restarts the count from 0; probe_broken = a broken probe is still unresolved, deleted only at a genuine release. The triage node deletes the stale clear_ticks, prev_poll_broken and probe_broken as its first act, so a new incident can NEVER inherit a banked count from the previous one.

defaults.context:
You are one lane of the incident-response workflow. Ground rules:
- SCRATCH DIR (shared handoff between lanes; create if missing with mkdir -p /tmp/incident-response-example): /tmp/incident-response-example/ holds incident.match (the incident fingerprint regex), verify_cmd.txt (the exact clear-check command the recovery gate polls - written once by triage), ticket.md (the tracking artifact: newest line wins; APPEND, never rewrite), analysis.md (correlate's write-up), timeline.log (milestone log - append one line per milestone).
- SWEEP: run {run.sweep_cmd} . With --expect clear it exits 0 iff NO firing alert matches the regex in incident.match; exit 1 = still firing; exit 2 = the probe itself broke (say so loudly, never report it as 'clear'; the recovery gate sticky-zeroes its counter on such a poll, so the next clear alone never releases it).
- Self-report is not proof: every claim you hand downstream must name the command/output that establishes it. The alert says a service is down - probe it LIVE before believing it.
- Notify channel: append to timeline.log. Wire your real notifier (webhook/IM) there in production.
- Keep answers to the schema; no narration. Never print secrets.

nodes.goal:
Incident triage. TRIGGER (reported by an operator/watchdog/webhook): {run.alert}
0) RESET THE DEBOUNCE: delete /tmp/incident-response-example/clear_ticks, /tmp/incident-response-example/prev_poll_broken and /tmp/incident-response-example/probe_broken before anything else (rm -f) — a leftover counter from a previous incident must never release this run's recovery gate.
1) Run {run.sweep_cmd} with a broad --match for a first look at everything firing.
2) The incident CLUSTER is anchored on the TRIGGER: firing alerts about the services/hosts it names, wherever they started. Use startsAt to build the timeline, never to drop trigger-matching alerts.
3) Write the fingerprint: the core services/hosts as a case-insensitive regex to /tmp/incident-response-example/incident.match. Then write the exact clear-check the recovery gate will poll: the sweep command with '--match' omitted (it then reads incident.match) plus '--expect clear', as a single line, to /tmp/incident-response-example/verify_cmd.txt. Re-run the sweep WITHOUT --match to confirm matched == the incident cluster and nothing unrelated (iterate the regex).
4) Check /tmp/incident-response-example/ticket.md for an OPEN ticket on this same condition; reuse it, else create it (one line: OPEN [incident] <symptom> (<services>)).
Reply with ONLY fenced json {"cluster": ["alertname@service", ...], "window": "<startsAt burst window>", "match_written": true, "reused": true|false, "notes": "<one line>"}

Causal correlation for the fingerprint in /tmp/incident-response-example/incident.match. Build the NARRATIVE and the CAUSE:
- Re-run {run.sweep_cmd} for the current firing set; group by host/service/startsAt burst.
- Change check: did a deploy, config push, or image bump land just before the burst touching these services or their dependencies? (git log in the ops repo, deploy tooling, recent restarts.)
- Other actors: anything else mid-flight on the box (provisioning runs, other agents, cron).
- LIVE dependency probe: the alert says down - prove or disprove it directly (health endpoints, process up, port answering). A dead monitoring agent produces fake incidents.
- Verdict: 'legit' (something actually broke), 'false_alarm' (services live and healthy; rule/threshold/window wrong), or 'real-external' (cause outside your control - upstream/ISP/physical).
- Write /tmp/incident-response-example/analysis.md (narrative, timeline, cause, evidence-per-claim, suggested mitigations). Append 'CORRELATE: <cause verdict + one line>' to ticket.md and timeline.log.
Reply with ONLY fenced json {"verdict": "legit|false_alarm|real-external", "cause": "<best-supported cause, one paragraph>", "narrative": ["<timeline line>", ...], "change_suspects": ["<commit/deploy/proc>", ...], "live_probe": "<what you probed and what it said>", "mitigations": ["<suggested action>", ...]}

FALSE-ALARM arm. Tune the offending alert rule so this condition stops paging (cause + live probe in correlate's output and /tmp/incident-response-example/analysis.md).
1) Find the rule (in your alerting rule files) matching the alertname; compare its threshold/window against the ACTUAL healthy values from your metrics source. Fix the root of the falseness (threshold, for-window, or a rule keyed on the wrong signal), not one number nudged past today's value.
2) Apply/reload the rule the way you normally converge monitoring config; verify via the alerting API that the new rule is live and the alert cleared.
3) Commit on a branch, merge per your repo policy. Append 'FALSE ALARM tuned: <rule, old->new, commit>' to ticket.md and timeline.log.
Reply with ONLY fenced json {"rule": "<id>", "old": "<expr/window>", "new": "<expr/window>", "commit": "<sha>", "cleared": true|false}

FALSE-ALARM closeout. Run /tmp/incident-response-example/verify_cmd.txt contents via the shell - it MUST exit 0. If the alert still fires (exit 1) or the probe broke (exit 2), do NOT close: append 'needs-drill: tune did not clear the alert (<detail>)' to ticket.md and report closed:false. When clear: append a CLOSED line to ticket.md (cause, tune diff + commit, verification evidence) and one line to timeline.log.
Reply with ONLY fenced json {"closed": true|false, "why": "<one line>"}

INCIDENT arm: troubleshoot and MITIGATE (mitigations in correlate's output + /tmp/incident-response-example/analysis.md).
- Work the mitigations in order of risk, least-disruptive first. BEFORE restarting anything that serves traffic, verify it is actually unhealthy - never restart a healthy-but-labeled workload.
- If the verdict is 'real-external' or no safe mitigation exists: STOP acting, append 'MITIGATION BLOCKED: <what is needed and why>' to analysis.md and ticket.md, and reply {"mitigated": false, ...}. Do not flail.
- Append one timeline line to ticket.md per action taken (with the command/output that proves it). Do NOT close the ticket; do NOT run broad config applies (a later node does that).
- When you believe the incident is mitigated, re-run {run.sweep_cmd} and report what it shows.
Reply with ONLY fenced json {"mitigated": true|false, "actions": ["<action + evidence>", ...], "blocked_reason": "<if mitigated=false>", "sweep_after": "<matched_firing count>"}

nodes.question: Incident alerts STILL firing 24h after the mitigation pass (or the probe itself broke). Extend another 24h, or stop and escalate to a human?

nodes.goal:
RECOVERY CONFIRMED by machine probe (two consecutive clear sweeps). Resiliency review: given the cause (correlate output + /tmp/incident-response-example/analysis.md), how did this fail, how long to notice, and what would make it self-heal or fail smaller next time? Candidate levers: restart/reschedule policy, check-window/threshold changes, a watchdog for the specific dependency that died, dependency-aware limits. Before proposing anything, check ticket.md and your tracker for follow-ups already covering each idea. Append 'RESILIENCY: <gap + follow-up id>' per real gap to ticket.md, and one line to timeline.log.
Reply with ONLY fenced json {"gaps": ["<gap + proposed fix>", ...], "followups": ["<id>", ...], "already_covered": ["<id>", ...]}

Convergence pass. 0) MERGE GATE FIRST: live state must equal your deploy branch. Enumerate every repo change this incident produced (mitigate/resiliency outputs + your repo's status + unmerged commits): each must be committed AND merged to your deploy branch BEFORE you converge anything - otherwise converge NOTHING for that change and record it in unmerged_refused[]. Converging an unmerged diff is forbidden: it makes live != main and the next incident's correlate lane reads a fiction. 1) Apply ONLY the affected config/services the normal way for your stack; never a blind whole-fleet apply. 2) POST-CONVERGE PROBE = one bounded machine re-check, NOT a sleep loop: /tmp/incident-response-example/verify_cmd.txt contents via the shell must exit 0, plus your live health probe for every service in the incident cluster - no converge may regress those. 3) Append 'CONVERGE+VERIFY: <roles applied + MERGED SHAs (not branch tips) + probe result>' to ticket.md and timeline.log.
Reply with ONLY fenced json {"drift": true|false, "merged_shas": ["<sha>", ...], "unmerged_refused": ["<change + why not converged>", ...], "converged": ["<role/service>", ...], "sweep_clear": true|false, "evidence": "<one line>"}

Close the incident ticket. GATE: converge.sweep_clear MUST be true and its evidence MUST show LIVE verification - if not, do NOT close: append 'needs-monitoring: <why>' to ticket.md and report closed:false. Otherwise append a CLOSED section to ticket.md (timeline, cause, mitigation, resiliency follow-ups, commits) and one final line to timeline.log.
Reply with ONLY fenced json {"closed": true|false, "why": "<one line: cause -> mitigation -> verified recovery>"}
